title: Integrating appreciative inquiry into architectural pedagogy
abstract: This paper evaluates pedagogical approaches for architecture students using appreciative inquiry. Outcomes focus on student learning and curriculum design rather than human cognitive or physiological responses to built environments.
label: NOT_RELEVANT

title: Global research agenda: Health, well-being, and the built environment
abstract: This research agenda synthesizes evidence linking built-environment features with human health and wellbeing, discusses mechanisms, and highlights research priorities for interdisciplinary work connecting architecture and health.
label: RELEVANT

title: Indicators of healthy architecture — A systematic literature review
abstract: A systematic review of architectural indicators associated with health outcomes. The review catalogs study designs, outcomes, and implications for design practice relevant to human physiological and psychological wellbeing.
label: RELEVANT

title: Quantifying thermal comfort and carbon savings from energy-retrofits in social housing
abstract: This study quantifies retrofit energy savings and occupant thermal comfort surveys. The primary contribution is engineering and energy analysis; occupant perceptions are secondary outcome measures.
label: NOT_RELEVANT

title: Hapticity in Hybrid Space from an Enactive Perspective
abstract: An enactive perspective on hybrid (virtual+physical) spaces, arguing for embodied interactions and sensory affordances that engage sensorimotor systems in architectural contexts.
label: RELEVANT

title: Seeing minds directly: Revisiting direct perception theory in social cognition
abstract: A theoretical paper revisiting direct perception theory in social cognition. The emphasis is on person-to-person perception rather than built-environment effects.
label: NOT_RELEVANT
